Return and Rehabilitation of Kashmiri Migrants 
*302.   SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:  
            DR. ABRAR AHMED:† 
Will the Minister of HOMEFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether any Action Plan for the return and rehabilitation of Kashmiri 
migrants have been prepared; and 
(b) if so, the status of the plan? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI HARIN PATHAK): (a) and (b) A statement is laid on the Table of the 
House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) In order to enable safe and honourable return of migrants to their 
native places in the Valley, the then State Government of J&K had finalized 
an Action Plan involving a total amount of Rs. 2589.73 crores. The Union 
Government has agreed to reimburse costs borne by tha State Government as 
per approved norms in the case of those 
†The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Dr. Abrar Ahmed. 
 
 
    1

RAJYA SABHA [12 March, 2003] 
Kashmiri migrants who actually return to the Valley.The Action Plan is to be 
implemented in phases which envisages return and rehabilitation of migrant 
families in areas where clusters of migrant houses are available and in 
villages/mohallas in the Kashmir Valle y Districts with sizeable Kashmiri 
Pandit population and where security is already being provided. To begin 
with, 166 houses forming 15 clusters were identified in Srinagar and Badgam 
Districts, which are considered safe for the return of the owners of these 
houses. The list of these clusters was published in the newspapers and steps 
were taken to identify the families and find their willingness to return to their 
homes. About 50 families who were registered with the Relief organisation, 
Jammu were contacted personally to give their consent for return to the 
Valley on the basis of the package announced by the Government. Interaction 
meetings with some of these families were also held but as reported by State 
Government, only two families (not belonging to the particular area) have 
agreed to return to the valley so far. 
The new State Government has indicated that it has identified the shrines 
in Mattan and Kheer Bhavani where the Kashmiri migrants displaced from 
these places could be settled temporarily by developing two model clusters 
containing temporary shelters for Kashmiri migrants, till such time they can 
repair their existing residential houses. Ministry of Finance has agreed to 
provide a grant of Rs. 10 crores to the State Government for the 
reconstruction/renovation of houses and shrines at Kheer Bhavani and 
Mattan.

Crimes against women 
*303.   DR.T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:† 
            SHRIMATI SHABANA AZMI: 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether in the year 2002, there had been increasing number of crimes 
against women; 
†The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Dr. T. Subbarami Reddy. 
5 

RAJYA SABHA [12 March, 2003] 
(b) if so, what were the main reasons for the same; 
(c) what are the efforts being made to reduce these crimes against women 
in 2003; 
 
(d) whether any proposals in this regard have been worked out; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI I.D. SWAMI): (a) to (e) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) The incidence of crime committed against women as reported in 
2000 were 1,41,373 which increased to 1,43,866 during 2001, thereby 
registering an increase of 1.8% during 2001 over 2000. 
(b) Poverty, work participation, social practices like dowry, the absence 
of gender sensitization, anonymity in urban areas and the physical vulnerability of 
women are some of the reasons for crime against women. 
(c) to (e) 'Police' and 'Public Order' are State subjects. Prevention of all 
crime including crime against women is primarily the responsibility of the 
State Governments. However, Government of India has been advising the 
State Governments from time to time to improve the administration of the 
criminal justice system and take such measures as are necessary for the 
prevention of atrocities against women and as a result of the overall efforts of 
the Central Government most of the State and the Union Territories have set 
up special cells to deal with crime against women. Many States have set up 
police stations managed exclusively by women police personnel to deal with 
crime related to women and also inculcate a sense of confidence and security in 
women to approach police stations without fear or apprehension. 
DR.T SUBBARAMI REDDY: Mr. Chairman, when I put the question, 
what are the efforts being made to reduce these crimes against women in 2003, 
the hon. Minister has said, 'It is a State subject. However, the Government of 
India has been advising the State Governments, from time to time.' I would 
like to put a straight question to not only the Hon. Minister but also the Hon. 
Deputy Prime Minister. In New Delhi, there 
6 

[12 March, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
have been so many crimes taking place against women particularly, recently, 
so many college students have been harassed, and also atrocities have taken 
place against women. I would like to know what protective measures the 
Government is taking at least, in New Delhi which is under the direct control 
of the Central Government, not merely telling that it is the responsibility of 
the State Governments. That is a different issue. So, I want a reply from the 
Hon. Deputy Prime Minister. Please tell us the measures. 
SHRI I.D. SWAMI: Sir. Not only in Delhi but also throughout the 
country, various measures have already been taken to ensure that the number 
of crimes against women does not increase, rather decreases, and the women 
feel a sense of security, 
So far as Delhi is concerned, in all the districts of Delhi, there are 
separate cells for women. These women cells have been created only to 
infuse enthusiasm and confidence in the women folk so that they can 
approach those cells easily. Various other measures, sensitisation, patrolling 
and all those things, in addition, are being taken, but more important is that 
for each district in Delhi, a separate women cell has been created so far that 
purpose. 
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: Sir, my second question in this. It has 
always been found that a number of people commit crimes against women and

Commission for Women have been taken in to consideration, and the criminal

already been appointed its report is expected very soon. But whatever 
recommendations that the National Commission for women has made, those 
have been seriously followed, and necessary action is being taken. That is 
right.For trial of crimes against women,  the concept of special court is also 
being envisaged.

THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI ANANT GANGARAM GEETE): (a) 
to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) According to the information received from Bharat Heavy 
Electricals Ltd., (BHEL) and Power Grid Corporation of India Limited 
(PGCIL), a prototype of "Controlled Shunt Reactor (CSR)" has been 
developed by BHEL. This CSR can be used selectively depending upon the 
system configuration and power system requirement. It aims to provide full 
reactive support to the lines during energisation and facilitate reactive power 
management in Extra High Voltage (E HV) power transmission system. The 
CSR is a significant development in the field of High Voltage Power 
Transmission as the use of this equipment is meant to improve the voltage 
profiles and reduce transmission losses. A prototype CSR of 50 MVAR  
capacity, 420 KV class developed by BHEL has been installed at 400 KV 
Itarsi sub-station of POWERGRID in September, 2001. 
(c) The requirement of CSR in the EH V system is mainly for controlling 
over-voltage where very fast control switching of reactor is desirable. 
Extensive studies are carried out to determine the size of the CSR and its 
location in the system, keeping in view its cost and requirement. Actual 
deployment of the CSR will depend on techno-economic considerations.

Demining in forward areas 
*301. SHRI K. RAHMAN KHAN: Will the Minister of DEFENCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that in the forward areas our forces are engaged 
in clearing mines without the aid of demining sets and mine boots; 
(b) if so, the number of Jawans killed and injured so far during the 
demining process; and 
(c) the steps proposed to be taken to stop manual demining to save 
human lives as well as complete the demining process quickly? 
THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES): (a) 
to (c) No, Sir. Demining equipment, anti-mine boots and other protective gear 
are available with our troops, who are engaged in demining operations in the 
forward areas, where land mines were laid during OPERATION 
PARAKARAM. Nevertheless, during the current demining operations, from 
October, 2002 upto 6th March, 2003, five Army personnel were killed and fifty-
nine were injured. 
Manual demining is an inescapable part of the demining process along 
with other methods, and thus cannot altogether be dispensed with. However, 
to ensure safety in demining operations, only trained army personnel who 
laid the mines and were familiar with the terrain, have been employed in 
recovery of the mines.

2230. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state:

taking action against illegal immigration from Bangladesh, Pakistan etc. 
and/or against overstay by foreign nationals; 
(b) the details of the States which are found to be failing in this regard; 
(c) whether they have explained the reasons to the Union Government 
for remaining soft on these issues inspite of its posing danger to the nation's 
security; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps initiated by Government to enable these States to 
effectively prevent, detect and deter unauthorized presence of foreigners in the 
country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI HARIN PATHAK): (a) to (d) All State Governments are taking 
action to detect and deport illegal foreign nationals including Bangladeshis 
and Pakistanis under delegated powers of the Foreigners Act, 1946, and these 
efforts have further been intensified. 
(e) To curb illegal influx into the country, several measures have been 
taken by the Government which include strengthening of BSF and equipping 
them with modern and sophisticated equipment/gadgets, raising of additional 
battalions of BSF; reduction of gaps between border outposts, intensification of 
patrolling, accelerated programme of construction of border roads and border 
fencing, provision of surveillance equipment etc. The powers under Section 
3(2)(c) of the Foreigners Act, 1946 to detect and deport foreign nationals 
staying in India unauthorisedly have been entrusted to the State Governments 
and UT Administrations. Besides administrative instructions are also issued to them 
from time to time to launch special drives to detect foreign nationals staying 
illegally in the country for their immediate deportation.

Acceleration of reforms in mining sector 
†2242. SHRI BALKAVI BAIRAGI: Will the Minister of MINES be 
pleased to state: 
(a) steps Government are going to take to accelerate the reform process 
in the mining sector; 
(b) whether the Government have incorporated aspects like scientific 
methods related to the mining sector, protection of the environment and 
implementing the programmes related to education, creation of jobs, health 
and environmental reforms for the people living in the adjoining areas of 
mines, on priority in the said programmes of reform-process; and 
(c) if so, the details therefor? 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
133 

RAJYA SABHA [12 March, 2003] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF MINES (SHRI 
RAMESH BAIS): (a) to (c) Implementati on of reform process in the mining 
sector is a continuous process. The National Mineral Policy (NMP) was 
announced in 1993 and the mining sector was thrown open for private 
investment including foreign investment. To give effect to the NMP and to 
take the reforms process forward extensive changes were made in the Mines 
and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 (MMDR Act) in 1994 
and 1999 and Rules framed thereunder were accordingly amended. 
The reform process encompassed inter alia opening up of the mining sector 
to private investment including foreign investment, delegation of powers to 
the State Governments, simplification of procedures, ushering in an investor-
friendly climate comparable with best global practices and ensuring 
systematic and scientific mining. 
Under the provision of Section 18 of the MMDR Act, 1957 Central 
Government have notified Mineral Conservation and Development Rules, 
1988 for conservation and systematic development of minerals and protection 
of environment. Appropriate penalties have been provided for contravention of 
these Rules. 
Interaction meetings with State Governments, Central Ministries/ 
Departments and the Investors in the mining sector are held from time to time 
to make the policy and procedure of grant of mineral concessions investor 
friendly and to sensitise the various stake holders about the reform process. 
Last three such meetings, a Tripartite meeting of Central Government, State 
Governments and Investors, 27th meeting of the Mineral Advisory Council 
and Conference of State Ministers of Mining and Geology have been held on 
12.11.2001, 21.9.2002 and 22.1.2003 respectively. 
In the process of ongoing consultation with the Stake-holders, it has been 
decided in the Conference of State Ministers of Mining and Geology held on 
22.1.2003 that for giving thrust to the mining sector reforms inter-alia for 
scientific methods related to mining protection of environment etc., the rules 
framed under the MMDR Act, 1957 shall incorporate provisions relating to 
minimum size of mining lease, and detailed provisions regarding mine closure 
plans and rehabilitation of mined out areas.

Adherence to safety norms 
2243. SHRI RAMACHANDRA KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of MINES 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the complete disregard for safety norms 
by the Geological Survey of India (GSI) resulting in many scientists and technical 
assistants facing life threatening diseases from radio-active chemicals they 
handle; 
(b) number of employees of CGD who died during last three years due to 
cancer and number of employees suffering from various skin diseases due to 
exposure to prolonged rediation; and

Regulatory Board norms during handling of chemicals such as cesium, Gamma 
and Nutron by the employees of Central Geophysical Division for exploration 
of minerals? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF MINES (SHRI 
RAMESH BAIS): (a) The Geological Surv ey of India (GSI) scientists and 
technical assistants always follow safety norms while handling hazardous 
radioactive chemicals and equipments which generate radiation. 
(b) No employee of GSI died or suffered from skin diseases due to 
exposure to such radiation during the last three years.

inspected the Central Geophysical Division of GSI in August, 2002 found that

aprons and radiation monitoring badges while handling chemicals and

Dabhol Power Project 
2260. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the details of investments made by Indian Financial Institutions/ 
Public Sector Banks in the Dabhol Power Corporation (DPC) both in equity of the 
company and as loan and year-wise disbursal of the same; 
(b) the present status of the DPC; 
(c) whether it has become commercially unviable project; and 
(d) if so, the measures taken and/or are contemplated to recover and secure 
the investments made by IFIs/Banks in the project? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA):(a) The Dabhol Power Project was 
constructed using a mix of equity and loan funds. The equity was brought in by 
the sponsors viz. Enron, General Electric, Bechtel and the Maharashtra Power 
Development Corporation Limited (MPDCL).The loan funds were advanced by 
a consortium of off-shore banks and Indian Financial Institutions/Banks 
(IFIs). The details of exposure of IFIs to Dabhol Power Company (DPC) 
(outstanding loans in respect of Phase-I and amounts disbursed plus balance to be 
disbursed in respect of Phase-ll 
163 

RAJYA SABHA [12 March, 2003] 
of the project) are indicated in Statement -I (See below). The details of year-
wise disbursement by IFIs are furnished in Statement- II (See below). The IFIs 
have not made any equity investment in the DPC. 
(b) to (d) Phase-I of the Dabhol plant (740 MW) has been shut down 
after the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) stopped taking power 
from 29th May, 2001, following disputes with Dabhol Company ~{DPC). 
Construction work on Phase-ll (1444 MW) has also been stopped. 
The Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) in regard to the Dabhol Power Project 
was entered into between MSEB and DPC. Thus, the responsibility to restart 
Phase-I and complete Phase-ll lies with the main stakeholders viz. MSEB and 
DPC as well as the Government of Maharashtra (GoM).The IFIs led by the Industrial 
Development Bank of India (IDBI) having substantial stakes in the Dabhol Power 
Project have been trying to restructure and revive the Dabhol plant. Government 
of India has agreed to facilitate and amicable solution to the various issues in 
order to revive/restructure the project. Any scheme finalised for revival of the 
Dabhol Project would come as a comprehensive package and would have to 
resolve complex, legal, financial and technical issues. While this may take time, 
as a first step, it has been agreed that an interim revival package for restarting 
Phase-I be workded out by the concerned agencies. The National Thermal 
Power Corporation (NTPC) has agreed to act as Operation and Maintenance 
Contractor for running Phase-I. A team involving representatives from NTPC, M's GE 
India, M/s Bechtel, IDBI, MSEB and Central Electricity Authority carried out a 
preliminary inspection of the Dabhol power plant from October 28-30, 2002 to 
ascertain its condition and to work out an action plan for restart of phase-l. 
During the visit, it was found, inter-alia, that the plant and equipments had generally 
been maintained well by the firm appointed by the Court receiver for maintenance 
and preservation of the assets. However, a more detailed assessment and internal 
inspection of the equipment is felt necessary so as to ascertain the time-frame for 
restarting the plant as well as the likely expenditure involved. 
Government of Maharashtra has taken a decision to allow MSEB to draw 
power from Phase-I at an optimum level of 83% at a tariff of about Rs. 
2.80/KWH on an interim basis subject to approval of the Maharashtra Electricity 
Regulatory Commission (MERC) and High Court of Maharashtra 
164 

[12 March, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
which has appointed a receiver for the project, and without prejudice to 
MSEB/GoM's rights and contentions in the pending arbitration/judicial and 
MERC proceedings. In a recent communication, GoM have stressed on the need 
to restart Phase-I of the Dabhol plant at the earliest keeping in view the acute 
power crisis being faced by the State. The viability of the project will depend 
on the final restructuring of the project and related issues such as cost of fuel, 
tariff levels and off-take of power, etc.

Assistant Secretary of Energy, Ms. Vicky Bailey, in her address at an

Power Business Community about the Power Sector in India on account of 
certain contratual and payment problems being faced by the existing 
Independent Power Producers (IPPs) with US investments. She observed that it

The main issue relates to the Dobhol Power Project which is an IPP set up

these two parties to the contract as well as the Government of Maharashtra, 
who have guaranteed the payment obligations of MSEB to DPC under the 
PPA, subject to final orders on the various legal proceedings, Government of 
India has agreed to facilitate any amicable solution to the various issues so as 
to revive/restructure the Dabhol Power Project.

Covanta Asia-Pacific and El Pasco India, during a recent meeting with 
Secretary (Power) discussed their problems with the Tamil Nadu Electricity 
Board relatiny to arrears, payment of invoices and establishing of security

creation of separate Land Resource Department vetted by the Planning

Level Committee on Wastelands Development headed by Shri Mohan Dharia 
in its report submitted in December 1995, recommended the creation of a

Resources and by the Ministries of Agriculture, Environment and Forests, and 
Planning Commission with different guidelines and varying financial patterns.

Watershed Development in the Department of Land Resources and to transfer to 
it various programmes and schemes relating to the conservation, development 
and management of land resources of the country.

Fluoride affected villages in Karnataka 
2299. SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that high fluoride content drinking water has 
disabled villagers in many parts of the State of Karnataka; 
(b) if so, the details of persons affected due to consumption of high 
fluoride content water, district-wise in the State for the past three years; 
(c) whether Government propose to make alternative supply of drinking water 
for the villages affected by fluoride contained water; and 
(d) If so, the details of the proposals and the estimated cost thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ANNASAHEB M.K. PATIL): (a) and (b) As 
reported by the State Government, 5838 habitations in 27 districts of 
Karnataka have fluoride contamination in drinking water affecting the 
inhabitants. The survey conducted in July 2000 in Nidasoshi village and 
another survey conducted in Keerunayaka Thanda village of Gulbarga district 
in 2002 have shown 7 and 18 persons affected by skeletal fluorosis respectively. 
This disability cannot be solely attributed to fluoride content in drinking water 
alone. 
(c) and (d) Rural drinking water is a State subject. State Governments take up 
schemes/projects for providing drinking water in rural areas from their own 
resources. Government of India supplements the efforts of the State 
Governments and provides financial assistance under Accelerated Rural Water 
Supply Programme (ARWSP). Under ARWSP, upto 15% of the allotted funds 
can be utilised to tackle water quality problem which inter-alia includes 
providing safe drinking water free from fluoride contamination. 
Government of India had been sanctioning projects under Sub Mission 
Programme for providing safe drinking water free from brackishness, 
214 

[12 March, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
fluorides, excess iron etc. till April, 1998. Since then, powers to approve and 
implement Sub Mission projects have been delegated to the State 
Governments. State Governments have repeatedly been requested to sanction 
more and more such projects to provide safe drinking water to rural 
habitations.

[12 March, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
schemes/programmes sanctioned for artisans is already in place. Various schemes 
being implemented in the handicrafts sector are continuously monitored by the 
Field Offices, Regional Offices and Headquarters Office of the Development 
Commissioner (Handicarafts). 
Statement 
Schemes in operation in handloom sector 
In order to ensure sufficient availability of yarn, which is the major raw 
material in handloom sector, the Government is implementing Mill Gate Price 
Scheme under which yam is supplied by National Handloom Development 
Corporation (NHDC) to handloom weavers and organizations at mill gate 
price. Government has also issued Hank Yarn Packing Notification under 
Essential Commodities Act 1955, which obliges yarn producers who pack yarn 
for civil consumption for sale/ transfer/delivery within the country have to 
pack at least 40% of the yarn in hank form. 
Further, in order to give continued protection to the handloom weavers, 
the State Government have been instructed to arrange distribution of bank 
yarn to handloom weavers, free of excise duty (CNVAT) through designated 
organizations which could clain reimbusrsement of the incidence of 
CENVAT borne by them on such yam from the Government of India. 
In order to provide adequate and timely credit facilities at concessional rate of 
interest, refinance assistance is being provided by National Bank for 
Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) to State Coopertive Banks 
for financing producftion and marketing activities of Primary Weavers, 
Cooperative Societies and for procurement and marking activities of Apex 
Weavers' Cooperative Societies. 
A scheme, namely Deen Dayal Hathkargha Protsahan Yojana, was 
introduced in the year 2000-2001 to cover entire gamut of activities from basic 
input and working capital to provisions of design, marketing, publicity etc. The 
Government of India has also been providing financial assistance for development 
of exportable products and their marketing, organisation of exhibitions, fairs, 
crafts melas, setting up of urban Haats, marketing complexes, publicity and 
awareness programmes. 
227 

RAJYA SABHA [12 March, 2003] 
Apart from this, the Government has set up National Centre forTextile Design 
(NCTD) to collate and disseminate all information related to textile weaves, 
fabric, colour, design etc. to act as an electronic forum to give the weavers 
design and marketing exposure. 
The Government has also promulgated the Handloom (Reservation of 
Articles for Production), Act, 1985 under which at present 11 categories of textile 
articles are exclusively reserved for production on handlooms. 
Health Package Scheme, Workshed-cum-Housing Scheme, Thrift Fund 
Scheme, Group Insurance Scheme and a New Insurance Scheme have been in 
operation for the welfare of handloom weavers. 
Besides, 24 Weavers' Service Centres are functioning to render extension 
services, which involve transfer of design inputs, skills and technology to the 
weavers. 
Schemes in operation in handicrafts sector 
The schemes include: "Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hastshilp Vikas Yojana 
(AHVY), training and extension, design and technical upgradation, marketing 
support and services, research- and development, financial assistance to state 
handicarafts development corporations/apex societies and export promotion etc. 
"Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hastshilp Vikas Yojana" (AHVY) seeks to develop 
selected artisan clusters into professionally managed self-reliant community 
enterprises working on the priciple of effective member participation and 
mutual cooperation and aims to achieve sustainable development of the 
artisan clusters. 
Besides, 52 Handicarafts Marketing & Service Extension Centres are 
functioning all over the country to assist the artisans in the area of marketing, 
raw material, credit facilities through financial institution and design 
development etc. Further, five Regional Design & Technical Development 
Centres (RD&TDC) undertake development and dissemination of new designs 
and improvement of tools and equipment. 
The Hon'ble Prime Minister had also announced in his address to the nation 
on August 15,2002 the facility of a one time special rebate @ 10% of the value 
of the handloom products sold, so as to enable the handloom sector to dispose of 
their stock and kick-start this employment intensive industry by reviving its 
production cycle. For this, a sum of Rs. 100 crore was announced. The State 
Government have already been instructed to

Modernisation of Textiles Industry 
2315. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether textile industry is modernising on massive scale to meet the 
global challenges, if so the details of such modernisation, as reported in the 
Economic Times on 17 December, 2002; 
(b) whether Government have received a good response for up-gradation 
from the Textile industry, if so, the total number of applications so far received 
and funds so far sanctioned under the Technology Upgradation Funds 
Scheme; and 
(c) incentives Government propose to extend for its growth and 
improvement of the yield to enable us to face world market? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES (SHRI 
BASANAGOUDA R. PATIL): (a) and (b) With a view to improve the overall 
viability of the textile and jute industries and to enable it to meet the global 
challenges, Government has launched a Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme 
(TUFS) for Textile and Jute Industries, w.e.f. 1.4.1999 for a period of 5 years, 
i.e. upto 31 st March 2004. The main feature of the scheme js that it provides a 
reimbursement of 5% point on the interest charged by the lending agency on a 
project of technology upgradation in conformity with this scheme.There is no cap 
on funding under this scheme. With effect from 1st Jan., 2002, an option has 
been provided to the Small Scale Textile and Jute Industries to avail of either 12 
percent Credit Linked Capital Subsidy (CLCS-TUFS) or 5 percent interest 
reimbursement under TUFS. 
232 

[12 March, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
As on December 31,2002, under the TUFS, 2023 applications have been 
received with a project cost of Rs. 15810 crore and a loan requirement of Rs. 9095 
crore. 1782 applications have been sanctioned for a loan amount of Rs. 6101 
crore. Rs. 4203 crore have been disbursed in respect of 1430 applications. 
(c) The Government has provided a number of incentives for the growth 
of textile sector and improvement of yield, which include:— 
i) Technology Mission on Cotton 
Government has launched the Technology Mission on Cotton during 1999-
2000 for a period of 5 years. This Mission has four Mini Missions to bring 
about all around improvement in the production, productivity and quality of 
cotton through research, transfer of technology and improvement in the raw 
cotton processing and marketing. 
ii) Textile Package in the Budget 2003-04 
In the current budget of 2003-04, to strengthen the textile industry, 
Central Value Added Tax (CENVAT) chain has been completed and the 
number of exemptions and deemed credit schemes have been withdrawn. 
The excise duty on fibres, yarn, fabrics/made ups and readymade garments 
(RMG) has been reduced considerably. 
iil) Reduction in Customs duty on Textile machinery 
In order to facilitate import of textile machinery with state of the art 
technology, list of 175 items of specified textile machinery attract 
concessional rate of import duty. In the current budget basic import duty on 
additional 39 numbers of textile machinery has been reduced to 5%. 
iv) De-reservation of Garment Industry and raising of Small Scale 
Industry (SSI) limit 
Garment industry has been de-reserved from SSI sector with effect from 
1st January, 2001 to encourage large-scale investments in the garment sector 
and achieving of economies of scale. Small-scale investment limit has been 
raised to Rs. 5 Crores in case of knitting and knitwear items. 
v) Integrated Apparel Park Scheme 
Governmet has formulated "Apparel Parks for Exports" with a view to 
involve State Government in promoting investment in the apparel sector. The 
Central Government will give as a grant 75% or maximum of Rs. 10 crore of the 
capital expenditure incurred by the State Government on the 
233 

RAJYA SABHA [12 March, 2003] 
infrastructure facilities of the Apparel Park, while the remaining 25% will be 
born by the agency. This grant shall be limited to a maximum of Rs. 10 crores. 
vi)Textile Centres Infrastructure Development Scheme (TCIDS) 
Government has launched Textile Centres Infrastructure Development 
Scheme (TCIDS)" for plugging critical infrastrcture gaps in traditional 
textile/apparel clusters to help the units located therein to become globally 
competitive. 
The central assistance under the scheme is available to the extent of 100% of 
the critical components of the project in respect of Common Effluent Plant, 
improving water supply and drainage facilities and construction of creche 
building for apparel units, whereas the other components would be funded on 
75:25 between Centre and State/reputed agencies concerned.

includes, modernisation, payment of statutory dues, secured loans, VRS to

would be given attractive VRS package. The remaining workers will continue 
in their jobs.

STATEMENT BY THE PRIME MINISTER REGARDING IRAQ SITUATION 
THE PRIME MINISTER (SHRI ATAL BIHARI VAJPAYEE) : Mr. 
Chairman, Sir, the situation relating to Iraq has been rapidly evolving over the 
past few weeks. India has consistently stood for a peaceful resolution of the 
Iraq issue. The peace and prosperity of the Gulf is of vital interest to India 
given our long standing political, cultural and economic ties with the countries 
of the region. There are over 3.5 million Indians working in the Gulf, whose 
welfare is of great concern to us. Their remittances are an important source of 
foreign exchange for the country. Over 60 per cent of India's crude oil imports 
are sourced from the region. The Gulf countries have also emerged as 
important destinations for our exports. 
India recognizes the validity of the unanimous decision of the UN 
Security Council in its Resolution 1441, which provides for the disarmament of 
Iraq and also reaffirms the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Iraq, Kuwait 
and the neighbouring States. Resolution 1441 provides a stringent regime of 
inspections designed to meet the international community's desire that 
Weapons of Mass Destruction are eliminated from Iraq. We believe that Iraq 
must cooperate actively with the inspection process and comply fully with all 
relevant Security Council Resolutions. If the pace of this cooperation had 
been quicker, it may have enabled United Nations Monitoring Verification and 
Inspection Commission and the International Atomic Energy Agency to certify 
to the UN Security Council that Iraq was in full compliance of Resolution 1441. 
The work of the inspectors is continuing in Iraq. The Security Council 
should decide on what further action needs to be taken. The international 
community must take a very careful look both at the objective of achieving 
Iraq's full compliance with UN resolutions and at the means to be adopted to 
reach this goal. This can best be achieved by a collective decision through the 
United Nations. If permitting more time and formulation of clearer criteria can 
facilitate a decision within the UN framework, we believe this option should be 
given a chance. We hope that the members of the Security Council will 
harmonise their positions to ensure that its final decision enhances the 
legitimacy and credibility of the United Nations. If unilateralism prevails, the 
U.N. would be deeply scarred, with disastrous consequences for the world 
order. The Government of India would strongly urge that no military action be 
taken, which does not have the collective concurrence of the international 
community. 
249 

RAJYA SABHA [12 March, 2003] 
India has voiced its concern on various occasions about the difficult 
humanitarian situation in Iraq. The Iraqi people have suffered severe 
shortages and hardships for over a decade. We have consistently stated that 
if Iraq complies fully with the provisions of relevant Security Council 
resolutions, then sanctions against that country should be lifted. 
While we sincerely hope, in the interest of all humanity, that the 
matter can be resolved peacefully through the United Nations, my Government 
has drawn up contingency plans to deal with any eventuality. There are less 
than 50 Indian nationals in Iraq at present and they have all been advised to 
leave the country in the coming days. It is unlikely that there would be any 
large scale dislocation of the Indian communities in the neighbouring countries 
on a possible outbreak of hostilities. Nevertheless the Ministry of Civil Aviation 
has drawn up plans to evacuate Indians, if necessary. The Ministry of 
Petroleum and Natural Gas has taken steps to shore up our inventories of 
crude oil. While no major dislocation in crude oil imports is envisaged, India 
has adequate foreign exchange reserves to meet a higher crude oil import bill 
if prices continue to rise in the short run. Thank you.
